correctness.rationale: In hyperbolic polar coordinates the inverse D_{1/a} has radial stretch 1/a and tangential stretch sinh(R/a)/sinh(R). For a>=1, sinh(R)>=a sinh(R/a), so D_{1/a} is globally 1/a-Lipschitz and D_a increases every pseudohyperbolic distance. Carleson's product-separation condition is therefore preserved. For 0<a<1, two-point packets at radii R_n with sin(theta_n/2)=c/sinh(R_n) have fixed source separation and can be spaced geometrically in boundary depth; the primary packet lemma makes their union interpolating, while the image separation tends to zero like sinh(aR_n)/sinh(R_n). The inverse identity D_a^{-1}=D_{1/a} then gives the exact bidirectional classification.

value.rationale: The source uses hyperbolic radius doubling as its canonical smooth witness separating one-way from bidirectional preservation. The accepted theorem completes that witness to the full natural multiplicative family and finds the exact phase boundary: a>=1 is precisely the forward-preserving cone, while bidirectional preservation leaves only the identity. This is a natural complete classification and semigroup structure theorem, not a numerical increment or arbitrary parameter slice.
